exposure: term not in labor (scheduled caesarian section)
preterm labor with rupture of membranes (PPROM)
outcome: connected pathways (kinase activation, NF-kB, inflammation, cytoskeletal remodeling, hormone regulation)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 13 patients (4 term not in labor, 3 vaginal term in labor, 3 PPROM, and 3 PTB) from whom fetal membrane and adjoining maternal decidua samples were collected.
finding: The study revealed spatially recognized differentially expressed genes aligned with four distinct gene clusters and their connected pathways (e.g., inflammation, hormone regulation) within the individual layers of the fetal membrane-decidual interface, showing unique contributions in term and preterm birth conditions.
mod_finding: Cluster 4 genes, containing AMC and CTC genes, were identified predominantly in term labor cases, distinguishing them from term not in labor (scheduled caesarian section).
cross-section timing: Samples were collected during scheduled caesarian section, vaginal term in labor, preterm labor with and without rupture of membranes.
gest_age: The study included both term (>=37 weeks) and preterm (<37 weeks) births, with preterm birth specifically defined as <37 weeks gestation.
